title: Constructors, Destructors and Object Lifecycle
learningObjectives: Explain constructors, destructors and object lifecycle.
Identify relevant class/object relationships and access rules.
Apply the OOP concept in a small design.

understand.concept: Constructors initialize objects; destructors run when object lifetime ends. Automatic objects are destroyed at scope exit, and member objects are destroyed in reverse declaration order.
understand.whyItMatters: Lifecycle understanding is essential for resource safety and predictable cleanup.
understand.explain: Initialize resources with RAII, avoid manual cleanup when possible, and understand destruction timing.

examples.title: Constructor initializes
examples.code: class Point{public:Point(int a,int b):x(a),y(b){}int x,y;};\nPoint p(2,3);
examples.explanation: Initializer list initializes members during construction.

examples.title: Destructor timing
examples.code: struct Notice{~Notice(){std::cout<<\"cleanup\";}};\n{Notice n;} // prints cleanup at block exit
examples.explanation: Destructor runs when automatic object's lifetime ends.

examples.title: Member destruction order
examples.code: struct A{};struct B{A first;A second;};\nB b; // second destroyed before first
examples.explanation: Members are destroyed in reverse declaration order.

examples.title: RAII wrapper concept
examples.explanation: The resource cleanup action is tied to object lifetime.

examples.title: Defaulted destructor
examples.explanation: Default destructor is sufficient when members manage themselves.

practise.guidedTask: Analyze the five Constructors, Destructors and Object Lifecycle examples. Identify class responsibilities, interface, object state, lifetime and dispatch behavior where relevant.
practise.independentTask: Design a small C++ program demonstrating constructors, destructors and object lifecycle in a practical domain. Use clear public operations, appropriate access control, and tests for expected behavior and edge cases.
hints: Start by listing responsibilities and objects.
Keep internal state protected where needed.
Initialize objects deliberately and understand lifetime.
Use inheritance only for substitutable relationships.
Test behavior through the public interface.

questions.explanation: Automatic objects are destroyed at scope exit.
Subobjects are destroyed in reverse declaration order.
RAII uses object lifetime for resource management.
Default destructor is fine for ordinary managed members.
